job.style: a news-style report about a real-world situation

response.passage: The historic lighthouse at Devil’s Point, built in 1894, has finally ceased its operations after 130 years of guiding ships along the Konkan coast. Local historian Mr. Arjun Rao explains that the lighthouse was decommissioned because the new satellite-based navigation systems make manual light signals redundant. For decades, the lighthouse keeper, Mr. Suresh Kulkarni, climbed the 85 spiral steps every evening to light the oil lamp. The structure has now been handed over to the Tourism Department to be converted into a museum. While many residents are sad, the local government believes this change will attract more visitors to the quiet village of Malvan. The lighthouse will remain standing as a monument to the maritime history of the region, though its rotating beam will no longer pierce the darkness of the Arabian Sea. Mr. Rao noted that the lighthouse survived three major cyclones, proving the strength of its original stone foundation. The transition is expected to be completed by December 2024, marking the end of an era for the coastal community.
response.summary: The 130-year-old lighthouse at Devil’s Point is closing down because modern technology has replaced its function. The site will be transformed into a museum to preserve its history for future visitors.
